original_text: –A scientific theoryis–much broader in scope than a hypothesis and –supported by a large and usually growing body of evidence.–Examples of 2 Fundamental Theories of Biology–Evolution–All living things have a common ancestor, but each is adapted to a particular way of life–Cell–All organisms are composed of cells, and new cells only come from pre-existing cells–When a theory is supported by all experimentation over a longer period of time, it may be referred to as a Principleor Law–Science is a social activity in which scientists–work in teams,–share information through peer-reviewed publications, meetings, and personal communication, and–build on and confirm each other’s work.
explanation: This slide distinguishes a scientific theory from a hypothesis, defining a theory as being much broader in scope and supported by a large, growing body of evidence. It lists two fundamental theories in biology: 1) The Theory of Evolution, which states that all living things share a common ancestor, but each species is adapted to a particular way of life; and 2) The Cell Theory, which states that all organisms are composed of cells, and new cells only arise from pre-existing cells. Over longer periods of time, when a theory is consistently supported by all experiments, it may be designated as a Principle or Law. Furthermore, the slide highlights that science is a collaborative social activity where scientists work in teams, share findings via peer-reviewed publications, meetings, and direct communication, and build upon and confirm one another's work.
